title: T1567.002: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
summary: Adversaries transfer data to a cloud storage service rather than to dedicated infrastructure, blending with sanctioned business use of the same services.
content:
## T1567.002 - Exfiltration to Cloud Storage

This entry covers an adversary behaviour observed in intrusions against provider organisations. Adversaries transfer data to a cloud storage service rather than to dedicated infrastructure, blending with sanctioned business use of the same services.

**Tactic:** Exfiltration

**Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS, SaaS

## Healthcare context

Provider organisations sanction cloud storage for research collaboration and administrative use, so the destination is already permitted and reputationally clean.

## Detection

Upload volume anomalies to storage domains per user; use of unsanctioned tenants within a sanctioned domain; transfers from hosts with no research or administrative role.

## Mitigations

- Restrict access to sanctioned tenants rather than to sanctioned domains.
- Baseline upload volume by user role.
- Deny cloud storage access from clinical host classes that have no business need.

## Notes for defenders

- Domain-level allowlisting is ineffective because the attacker uses the same domain as the business.
- Tenant-level restriction is the control that actually separates sanctioned from unsanctioned use.
- This technique underpins the exfiltration half of double-extortion ransomware.
